analysis:
Examined the add-on hold hardening (TB-012, A-018, T-059 and new T-060) across the YAML head text, AddonHoldStore.swift and AddonIPCServer.swift. No regression found.

AddonHoldStore.read (head line 27) now opens with O_NONBLOCK. A FIFO at the hold-record path no longer blocks the open or read. The existing fstat checks (owner uid, S_IFREG, mode & 0o077 == 0, size bound) then return .invalid. O_NOFOLLOW is retained. The write path (atomic rename, 0600, O_EXCL) is unchanged.

AddonIPCServer now verifies the peer at accept (head lines ~136-138), before the peer takes one of the 8 slots. It reuses the same AddonPeerPolicy.peerToken and authenticate path, so an unsigned peer cannot hold a slot. Per-request re-verification is kept in respond(), so the TOCTOU defense against a peer that later executes other code is not weakened. refuseUnadmitted closes only fds never inserted into `connections`, so it cannot race stop(). Its single small write to a fresh socket is bounded by a 5s timeout.

The new 10s requestTimeout (lineStarted, lines ~167-182) is anchored at the first buffered byte and cleared only when a full line is consumed. Trickling bytes cannot extend it. The size cap is preserved and merged into the same check.

Residual and accepted: verification now runs serially on the accept thread. A same-UID flood of connections could delay the add-on's accept, which T-060 records as accepted. Legitimate verified add-on connections still hold a slot up to the 300s idle timeout, which is acceptable since only signed peers get one.

T-060's claims about LifecycleMailbox O_NONBLOCK/O_NOFOLLOW reads, the mailbox, the socket override and the fail-open hold record rest on files not supplied here (the YAML diff was truncated at TB-012). I could not verify those, so the next pass should check them against LifecycleMailbox.swift and ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift. T-060 lists ADV-003 (external attacker) for what is a same-UID local threat; that is a minor documentation imprecision.
